title: [Idea] a playlist for audio and video

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
It really feels like a `<video>` is missing a playlist. media libraries often have to reinvent the wheel and create some sort of playlist from scratch and having there own way of solving things by listening to end-events 

Sometime you want to play a list of episodes out of a TV-serie or listen to some album

I think it's time that the media player got native support for some sort of playlist/queue that can be created with regular HTML, manipulated with some sort of javascript, and gets native controller for prev, next, shuffle with the native video controller and even somehow being able to select a item in the queue if that is possible to squeeze in some how in the UI

If you decide to implement some kind of playlist on your own then the result is likely going to be that you override the hole native video controller just so that you can add some missing prev/next button, which in the end result in reinventing play/pause/volume/pip etc...

Some recommendation: 

```html
<queue id="myPlaylist" shuffle>
  <item index="0">
    <source src="flower.webm" type="video/webm">
    <track default kind="captions" srclang="en" src="flower.vtt" />
  </item>
  <item index="1" active>
    <source src="bigbuck.webm" type="video/webm">
  </item>
</queue>

<video queue="myPlaylist" />
<audio queue="myPlaylist" />
```

and some sort of javascript api:
```js
const [queueList, video] = document.querySelectorAll('queue, video')
video.queueJump(-1) // prev
video.queueJump(1) // next
queueList.add(...)
queueList.remove(...)
queueList.shuffle = false
queueList['at' || 'item'](3).active = true
```

I have absolutely no idea how a grate api would look like, but need to start somewhere just to get the ball rolling and brainstorm some ideas. could take some ideas from pre existing libraries also

I mean, it feels weird that you can add native functionality for Next Track in MediaSession
```js
navigator.mediaSession.setActionHandler('nexttrack', handler)
```
...But you have to build a playlist on your own. It would have been nice if the MediaSession could hook into the video/playlist somehow and knowingly figure out if there is a next/prev track or if it's playing something or not or what the current time is. but i understand if it has to be decoupled from the media entirely if you don't use the audio or video (such as flash and audio context, canvas)
Makes me wonder if not the playlist or the video/audio would need some event listener also for when it switch track

---

ChromeCast receiver have this virtual playlist where you can resolve a promise when calling prev/next so you don't have to load the hole playlist. You can also define how many items there is in the queue and where in the queue you are
